title: Decide whether heat-exchanger data can identify a model
equipment: Plate heat exchanger with three independent simulated experiment copies
physicalPurpose: Reject weak or feedback-correlated records before an ordinary open-loop estimator presents their parameters as trustworthy.
principalTechnique: Data identifiability and closed-loop correlation qualification
objective: Compare weak open-loop, qualified open-loop, and ordinary feedback records and retain a deterministic qualification decision for each.

simplifications: One local steady gain, one dominant lag, and one transport delay
Independent deterministic measurement-noise stream for each plant copy
Fixed flow, inlet temperatures, heat-transfer coefficient, valve dynamics, and fouling

baseline.limitation: Finite fitted values can look credible even when weak excitation or feedback correlation makes their interpretation invalid.

change.decision: Retain every record but allow the ordinary open-loop identification route only when amplitude, duration, quality, and independence checks pass.

disturbances: Independent deterministic outlet-temperature measurement noise on every plant copy

acceptance.window: final 10 s after at least 63 s
final 10 s of the 70 s enabled record; dynamic-window evidence, not a settled claim
qualification result derived from the complete poor record
qualification result derived after at least 63 s
qualification result derived from the complete ordinary feedback record

abortPredicates: Any required sample is nonfinite or has invalid quality
Any required sample is missing or the interval changes
Temperature drift or an unreviewed disturbance invalidates the common baseline
The heat exchanger leaves its declared local operating region
safety.restorationMode: Set ExperimentEnabled false, restore every valve to 20 percent, and observe return toward 50 degC
safety.physicalApprovalRole: authorised process controls engineer and heat-exchanger operator
simulationOnlyRestrictions: This project cannot authorise physical valve excitation
Physical testing requires reviewed pressure, temperature, flow, valve authority, interlocks, operating procedure, personnel protection, and explicit immediate approval

video.viewerOutcome: Reject weak and feedback-correlated data before fitting an ordinary open-loop model.

learning.context: Three independent simulated copies of one plate heat exchanger provide weak open-loop, qualified open-loop, and ordinary feedback records.
learning.reason: Model selection assumes that the estimation data can distinguish the parameters, but finite fit output does not prove identifiability.
theory: Identifiability requires observable parameter effects above noise and across the needed experiment bandwidth.
Input span, expected response, noise, SNR, duration, quality, and exogenous excitation are qualified before fitting.
Ordinary feedback makes valve input depend on the noisy measured output, violating an ordinary open-loop estimator's independence assumption.
learning.workedPrediction: Predict poor-step SNR 0.67 and reason 1, qualified-step equilibrium movement 5 degC, about 4.75 degC movement at 63 s, SNR 33.33 and reason 0, and feedback correlation magnitude at least 0.95 with reason 2.
practicalPreparation: Verify Simulation evidence, three plant copies, requested and applied signals, controller-used measurement, units, quality, limits, noise, 100 ms sampling, operating point, and seed.
Record qualification thresholds and expected decisions before enabling the experiment.
learning.baseline: Attempting to fit weak or ordinary feedback data can return plausible parameters without establishing their meaning.
learning.change: Apply deterministic data qualification before the ordinary open-loop fitting route and retain every accepted or rejected record.
learning.comparison: Compare applied-input span, response, SNR, duration, quality, exogenous-input status, correlation, and deterministic reason under declared conditions.
learning.validation: Require poor 0.2-point span, 0.1 degC predicted equilibrium response, SNR 0.67 and reason 1; qualified 10-point span, 5 degC predicted equilibrium response, about 4.8 degC measured late response, SNR 33.33 and reason 0; feedback correlation at most -0.95 and reason 2.
learning.explanation: Weak excitation hides parameter effects inside noise, while feedback creates causal input-noise dependence that violates the open-loop method's assumption.
learning.transfer: Return Data inadequate with retained evidence when assumptions fail; Lesson 41 tests whether a qualified fitted model predicts independent conditions.
